newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Commissioner says Clinton harassed EU on Boeing.
newsitem.headline: EU Commissioner says Clinton harassed EU on Boeing.

text.p: European Commissioner Edith Cresson on Thursday accused U.S. President Bill Clinton of harassing European Union leaders to win EU approval for a merger between aerospace giants Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.

"This American pressure is quite inadmissible," EU Research Commissioner Cresson told France Inter radio a day after the Commission formally blessed the $15 billion merger that averted a transatlantic trade war.
"Mr Clinton telephoned several heads of state and government leaders. (It's) quite abnormal, absolutely abnormal," she said.
"He called the Prime Minister of Luxembourg (Jean-Claude Juncker) -- Luxembourg has the EU's presidency at the moment -- at two o'clock in the morning," Cresson said.

Cresson, a former French prime minister who said last week that she disagreed with the EU's preliminary approval, said the issue was now closed with the green light given by the 20-member Commission on Wednesday.
"This is a great American victory," she said. The merger will form the world's largest aerospace company.
"I note that we collectively bowed to an American will for hegemony, but we retain some trumps...firstly, the challenger to this semi-monopoly which is Airbus," she said.
"We must do everything to ensure that this challenger is as vigorous as possible," she added.

Cresson said Europe had obtained some important concessions, notably a pledge from Boeing not to enforce exclusivity contracts in long-term supply contracts. But she said the EU had failed to win a sell-off of parts of McDonnell Douglas.
"When there is a very important concentration, not to say a semi-monopoly, it's normal in competition law to ask for...the sale of part of the whole," she said.
After the merger, Boeing's share of the commercial jet market will increase to 70 percent from its current level of 64 percent, leaving only Airbus in a position to compete.
